identity.title: Extended Millimeter Emission in the HD 141569 Circumstellar Disk Detected with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: Our analysis uses three archival ALMA data sets and a PSF subtracted HST scattered light image from (cite: konishi).

evidence.quote: corresponding to $\sim 112$ au at the system distance of 111 pc.

question.value: Is there extended millimeter emission exterior to the inner disk of HD 141569, and how do the grain size distributions of the inner and outer disks compare?

evidence.quote: These data detect extended millimeter emission that is exterior to the inner disk.
The ALMA observations are at 345 GHz (ID 2012.1.00698.S)
We present archival ALMA observations of the HD 141569 circumstellar disk at 345, 230, and 100 GHz.

evidence.quote: two SPWs had 2000 MHz bandpasses centered at rest frequencies of 231.02 and 233.02 GHz.
The size of the resulting synthesized beam is $1.03 \times 0.99$ arcsec$^{2}$ at a position angle of 70.8$^{\circ}$
The 230 GHz observations achieve a sensitivity of $130~\mu \rm Jy~beam^{-1}$.

method.value: Annular averaging of visibilities for each frequency

evidence.quote: The visibility data for each frequency is annularly averaged in 10-k$\lambda$ bins

key_parameters.value: 10 klambda bins; uncertainty is the standard deviation per bin

evidence.quote: The uncertainties represent the standard deviation of each bin.

method.value: MCMC fit of a surface brightness ∝ r^-1 disk with inner and outer edges to all three data sets at once

evidence.quote: The single-component model used here adopts a surface brightness profile $\propto r^{-1}$ and assumes the disk has an inner and outer edge.

key_parameters.value: Free: 345 GHz flux, spectral index, disk center, width; uniform priors flux 0.01-50 mJy, disk 0.1-300 au, index 0-4

evidence.quote: A uniform prior distribution is chosen for the flux to range from .01 to 50 mJy, the disk from 0.1 to 300 au, and the spectral index from 0 to 4.

assumptions.value: Flux follows a single power law in frequency

evidence.quote: (and assuming the flux is well defined by a single power law in frequency)

fitting.value: Metropolis-Hastings MCMC; chi2 averaged with equal weight over the three frequencies

evidence.quote: The three are averaged together with equal weighting to get a representative $\chi^{2}$.

validation.value: Jeffreys priors gave negligible differences; uniform-disk fit consistent with uvmodelfit

evidence.quote: we ran MCMC modeling for the single component using Jeffreys priors, which resulted in negligible differences.

method.value: MCMC fit of inner and outer disks, each with own center, width and spectral index; non-overlapping

evidence.quote: The inner disk prior range is from 0.1 to 100 and the outer disk prior range is from 50 to 500 au, and models are not accepted if the two disks overlap.

fitting.value: Same MCMC; most probable values and 95% credible regions

evidence.quote: A summary of the most probable model parameters, 95% Credible Region, and reduced $\chi^{2}$ at each frequency are given in Table [\[obs\]](#obs).

validation.value: Compared reduced chi2 of the models

evidence.quote: the two-component model is preferred (1.74 versus 1.08 averaged reduced $\chi^{2}$)

method.value: Sum flux in elliptical apertures from images, normalize and compare with HST

evidence.quote: These curves were generated by summing up the total flux in elliptical apertures with the inclination and position angle previously constrained in the disk (cite: white16).

validation.value: Check for a slight peak consistent with visibility-modeled outer disk

evidence.quote: the slight peak in flux is broadly consistent with the 95 - 300 au outer disk location detected in the visibility data.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive grain size distribution slope q

evidence.quote: q = \frac{\alpha_{mm} - \alpha_{pl}}{\beta_{s}} + 3,
where $\beta_{s} = 1.8\pm0.2$ is a power law index for the dust opacity (cite: draine)

method.value: Optically thin single grain size mass, and a full size distribution mass for 10 um to 3 mm grains

evidence.quote: assume the disk is populated only by grains that have been observed (i.e. $\sim~10~\mu$m to $\sim~3$ mm).

evidence.quote: The adopted stellar parameters are $T_{*} = 10500$ K, $L_{*} = 24.2~\rm L_{\odot}$, and $d=111$ pc.

The inner disk ranges from approximately 16 to 45 au

results_numeric.quantity: Average reduced chi2 single vs two-component
Mass in 10 um-3 mm solids, inner and outer disk

For the outer disk, the best fit 345 GHz flux is 11 mJy

findings_qualitative.value: The outer disk's grain size distribution is steeper than the inner disk's; the radial profiles give only tentative support.

evidence.quote: HD 141569’s outer disk has a steeper grain size distribution than the inner disk.

claims.hypothesis: Millimeter emission exists exterior to the inner disk of HD 141569
claims.experiment: Simultaneous MCMC visibility fits of one- and two-component models to 345, 230 and 100 GHz data
claims.result: Two-component model has average reduced chi2 of 1.08 vs 1.72; outer disk at 95-300 au
claims.finding: Extended mm emission is detected in the outer disk

evidence.quote: the system’s morphology is described well by a two-component disk model.

claims.hypothesis: The outer disk has a more evolved grain size distribution
claims.finding: Outer disk has a steeper q, so is more evolved

evidence.quote: grain size distribution is steeper, and therefore more evolved, in the outer disk than in the inner disk.

limitations_admitted.value: Equal weighting of frequencies may not reflect each data set's beam and sensitivity; image plane detection not convincing

evidence.quote: an equal weighting of each frequency may not directly reflect the contribution from each set of visibilities.

referee_caveats_inferred: Outer disk detection rests on a modest chi2 improvement, and the 230 GHz data are noisy
Spectral index uncertainties are large and overlap between protoplanetary and debris values
Dust temperature for alpha_pl is not given

data_public_as_stated.value: Archival ALMA data retrieved from the archive

evidence.quote: The 230 GHz ALMA data were retrieved from the ALMA archive.

reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and a clear model, but MCMC settings, geometry and the temperature assumption are missing, and the method is inherited from earlier papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data and numeric results, but the recipe has gaps.
